question: What does a general liability policy exclude, and which exclusions have a way back in?
aliases: CGL exclusions list a through q
does general liability exclude professional services
damage to your work subcontractor exception
does general liability cover employee injuries
shortAnswer: Coverage A carries seventeen exclusions, lettered a. through q. [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13], and several of them contain their own exception, so reading the exclusion without reading its final sentence gives the wrong answer. Two facts are worth having up front. This base form's Coverage A exclusions do not include a professional services exclusion [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13], so where one exists it has been endorsed on. And the Damage To Your Work exclusion does not apply where the damaged work, or the work out of which the damage arises, was performed on the named insured's behalf by a subcontractor [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
assumes: The policy uses the standard Commercial General Liability Coverage Form as published in the April 2013 edition [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. Endorsements add and remove exclusions and the policy issued governs.
You are asking about Coverage A. Coverage B has its own separate exclusions, including its own pollution exclusion [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
You are asking what the form excludes, not whether a particular claim falls inside an exclusion, which is decided on the facts.
why:
The list runs: Expected Or Intended Injury; Contractual Liability; Liquor Liability; Workers' Compensation And Similar Laws; Employer's Liability; Pollution; Aircraft, Auto Or Watercraft; Mobile Equipment; War; Damage To Property; Damage To Your Product; Damage To Your Work; Damage To Impaired Property Or Property Not Physically Injured; Recall Of Products, Work Or Impaired Property; Personal And Advertising Injury; Electronic Data; and Recording And Distribution Of Material Or Information In Violation Of Law [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].

What is absent matters as much. The Coverage A list in this base form does not include a professional services exclusion [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. So a professional services exclusion on a real policy is an endorsement, and the question to ask is which endorsement and how broadly it is drafted.

Several exclusions carry a way back in, and these are where most of the useful reading is.

Expected Or Intended Injury does not apply to bodily injury resulting from the use of reasonable force to protect persons or property [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. That is stated in the same paragraph as the exclusion, which is exactly why it is missed.

Contractual Liability removes bodily injury or property damage the insured is obligated to pay by reason of assuming liability in a contract, but does not apply to liability the insured would have had in the absence of the contract, nor to liability assumed in an insured contract, provided the injury or damage occurs after the contract was executed [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. Insured contract is a defined term covering a lease of premises with a fire-damage carve-out, a sidetrack agreement, an easement or licence agreement with a railroad exception, an obligation required by ordinance to indemnify a municipality with a stated exception, an elevator maintenance agreement, and that part of any other contract pertaining to the insured's business under which the insured assumes the tort liability of another party for bodily injury or property damage to a third person [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. Solely for liability assumed in an insured contract, reasonable attorneys' fees and necessary litigation expenses incurred by or for a party other than an insured are deemed damages, provided that party's defence was also assumed in the same insured contract and the fees are for defending a proceeding in which covered damages are alleged [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].

One caution that belongs with it, because the confusion is common and the form settles it: nothing in the Contractual Liability exclusion or its insured contract exception amends Who Is An Insured or confers additional insured status [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. An insured contract is not an additional insured endorsement.

Liquor Liability has the most surprising limit of the seventeen. It removes injury or damage for which any insured may be held liable by causing or contributing to intoxication, furnishing alcohol to someone underage or already under the influence, or by any statute relating to the sale, gift, distribution or use of alcohol [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13], and it applies even where the claim alleges negligence in supervision, hiring, employment, training or monitoring, or in providing or failing to provide transportation for a person who may be under the influence [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. But it closes with a limiting clause: it applies only if the named insured is in the business of manufacturing, distributing, selling, serving or furnishing alcoholic beverages, and permitting a person to bring alcohol onto the premises for consumption there, whether or not a fee is charged or a licence is required, is not by itself that business [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. So an office party where people bring their own is not caught by this exclusion on the strength of the drinks alone.

Employer's Liability reaches bodily injury to an employee arising out of and in the course of employment or of duties related to the insured's business, and to that employee's spouse, child, parent, brother or sister as a consequence, applying whether the insured is liable as an employer or in any other capacity and to any obligation to share damages or repay someone else [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. Then its exception: it does not apply to liability assumed by the insured under an insured contract [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].

Pollution excludes injury or damage arising out of the actual, alleged or threatened discharge, dispersal, seepage, migration, release or escape of pollutants at or from premises the insured owns, occupies, rents or borrows, and at or from premises where the insured or its contractors are performing operations if the pollutants were brought on in connection with those operations, subject to stated exceptions [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. One of those exceptions is bodily injury sustained within a building caused by smoke, fumes, vapor or soot produced by or originating from equipment used to heat, cool or dehumidify the building [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. A separate paragraph excludes clean-up costs arising out of a request, demand, order or statutory requirement to test for, monitor, clean up, remove, contain, treat, detoxify or neutralise pollutants, or a claim by a governmental authority for such damages [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13] and then provides that it does not apply to liability for property damage the insured would have had in the absence of that request, demand, order, requirement or claim [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].

The business-risk group is where contractors and manufacturers live. Damage To Your Product removes property damage to the insured's product arising out of it or any part of it, and carries no stated exception in this form [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. Damage To Your Work removes property damage to the insured's work arising out of it and included in the products-completed operations hazard, except where the damaged work, or the work the damage arises out of, was performed on the named insured's behalf by a subcontractor [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. That subcontractor exception is the single most consequential sentence in this group for a general contractor. Damage To Impaired Property removes property damage to impaired property or to property not physically injured arising out of a defect, deficiency, inadequacy or dangerous condition in the insured's product or work, or out of a delay or failure to perform a contract, except for loss of use of other property arising out of sudden and accidental physical injury to the product or work after it has been put to its intended use [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. Recall removes loss, cost or expense for the loss of use, withdrawal, recall, inspection, repair, replacement, adjustment, removal or disposal of the insured's product, work or impaired property, and applies only where it is withdrawn or recalled because of a known or suspected defect, deficiency, inadequacy or dangerous condition [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].

Three more are worth naming. Electronic Data removes damages arising out of the loss of, loss of use of, damage to, corruption of, inability to access or inability to manipulate electronic data, and states in the same paragraph that it does not apply to liability for damages because of bodily injury [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. War excludes injury or damage arising directly or indirectly out of war including undeclared or civil war, warlike action by a military force, and insurrection, rebellion, revolution, usurped power or action by governmental authority in hindering or defending against any of these [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. And exclusion q. excludes injury or damage arising directly or indirectly out of any action or omission that violates or is alleged to violate the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, the CAN-SPAM Act of 2003, the Fair Credit Reporting Act including its Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act amendment, or any other similar statute [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
whatChanges: Whether the damaged work was performed by a subcontractor, which is the exception to the Damage To Your Work exclusion [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Whether the liability was assumed in an insured contract, which is the exception to both Contractual Liability and Employer's Liability [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Whether the named insured is in the business of manufacturing, distributing, selling, serving or furnishing alcohol, since the Liquor Liability exclusion applies only then [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Whether pollution injury was sustained inside a building from heating, cooling or dehumidifying equipment, which is a stated exception [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Whether a pollution claim is for clean-up demanded by an authority or for property damage the insured would have owed anyway [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Whether an electronic data claim includes bodily injury, which the exclusion does not reach [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Whether a professional services exclusion has been endorsed on, since the base form has none [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
variability: This describes the base form as published in the April 2013 edition [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13]. Endorsements routinely add exclusions, including professional services, and remove or narrow the exceptions described here. The policy issued governs.

Whether a claim falls inside an exclusion or inside its exception is decided on the facts and on the defined terms, several of which this record does not set out in full, including products-completed operations hazard, your work, your product and impaired property.
Coverage B carries its own exclusions, including its own pollution exclusion [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13], and nothing here describes them.
The absence of a professional services exclusion from the base list [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13] is a statement about this form, not about any market policy.
nextActions: Read the endorsement schedule before the exclusions, since the most consequential exclusion on a real policy is often one the base form does not contain [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
If you are a general contractor, check that the subcontractor exception to Damage To Your Work has not been endorsed away [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Read the last sentence of any exclusion you are relying on, because several state their own exception in the same paragraph [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
If you host events with alcohol, establish whether you are in the alcohol business as the exclusion defines it rather than assuming the exclusion applies [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Do not treat an insured contract as conferring additional insured status, which the form says it does not [S:iso-cg-00-01-04-13].
Where a denial rests on an exclusion with an exception, put the exception to the insurer in writing by name.
author: Aaron Bollinger

handoff.reason: Almost every question here turns on a defined term or on the facts of a loss, and on a real policy the operative exclusion is frequently one endorsed on rather than one in the base form. Reading the endorsement schedule against the exposure is broker work.
